title: Crystallize kernel provenance index and fastpath validation for safe GPU runtime upgrades
creator: Lena Patel
description: Background: Upgrading CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA stacks in mixed hardware fleets has repeatedly caused subtle symbol-resolution and behavioral mismatches that surface as rare inference regressions and cold-start failures. This ticket creates a deterministic kernel provenance index plus an inline fastpath validation step that runs during node bootstrap and during staged rollouts. The goal is to provide a lightweight, auditable record (hash + provenance metadata) for every kernel bundle and a fast validation that can detect incompatible ABI/semantics before the node begins serving production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: A hashed provenance index (sha256) is generated for every kernel bundle produced by our build pipeline and uploaded as a signed artifact alongside the bundle in GCS.
Node bootstrap reads index entry and performs an O(1) fastpath validation (symbol table fingerprint + lightweight smoke-run) that returns PASS/FLAG/FAIL within 5s on warm instances.
CI gate includes a validator job that runs validation against the current canary fleet image and fails the PR if compatibility regressions are detected.
Rollout tooling can automatically mark nodes as 'quarantined' when validation returns FLAG and route traffic away until operator approval or rollback completes.
Telemetry emits validation outcome, kernel-hash, and short stacktrace for any FLAG/FAIL with retention in dashboard for 90 days.
No measurable increase in steady-state cold-start latency for our smallest GPU shapes (>99th percentile baseline +/- 5ms acceptable).
Docs and runbook updated with rollback steps, how to interpret validator output, and an example incident playbook.
Security review completed for signed index (KMS signing flow) and keys provisioned in staging.

notes: Risk: false negatives are worse than false positives for safety; validator defaults to FLAG (route away) to prevent bad upgrades. Rollout plan: enable validator in staging -> run 24h smoke canary on internal traffic -> enable 5% external traffic with auto-routing on FLAG -> increase to 25% after 48h. Follow-up tickets will address binary delta patches and automated grafting. Ownership: runtime + infra; coordinate with release engineering for signing key rotation.
